# Server-side request to a URL from HTTP request data (C#)

`qualor:csharp/ssrf` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-918](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/918.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A01:2025 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A01_2025-Broken_Access_Control/), [A10:2021 Server-Side Request Forgery](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A10_2021-Server-Side_Request_Forgery_%28SSRF%29/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data in ASP.NET Core (MVC and Web API controllers, Minimal APIs, Razor Pages) that
chooses the URL of a request the server itself makes:

- the URL given to `HttpClient`'s `GetAsync`, `GetStringAsync`, `GetByteArrayAsync`,
  `GetStreamAsync`, `PostAsync`, `PutAsync`, `PatchAsync`, `DeleteAsync` and the JSON extensions
  (`GetFromJsonAsync`, `PostAsJsonAsync`, ...), on an `HttpClient` field, parameter or local, on a
  client from `IHttpClientFactory.CreateClient`, or on `new HttpClient()`;
- the URL of an `HttpRequestMessage` (constructor or `RequestUri`), a client's `BaseAddress`, and
  `WebRequest.Create`, `WebRequest.CreateHttp` and `HttpWebRequest.Create`.

A URL is reported when request data can set its scheme or host: the value used as it is, wrapped
in `new Uri(...)` or a `UriBuilder`, or appended to a base without a separator after the host
(`"https://api.example.com" + city`, where `@evil.example` changes the host). Request data after a
fixed origin and a separator (`"https://api.example.com/items/" + id`, `$"v1/items/{id}"`), or
percent-encoded with `Uri.EscapeDataString`, is not reported.

Request data means the parameters of controller actions, Razor Pages handlers and Minimal API
handlers (strings, string arrays, `StringValues`, forms, uploaded files, the body stream, and any
parameter bound with `[FromQuery]`, `[FromRoute]`, `[FromForm]`, `[FromHeader]`, `[FromBody]` or
`[AsParameters]`), `[BindProperty]` properties, and the request object itself (`Request.Query`,
`Form`, `Headers`, `Cookies`, `RouteValues`, `Body`, ...).
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
The server usually sits inside a network that the client cannot reach. If a request decides where
the server sends its own requests, an attacker can reach internal services and admin interfaces,
read cloud metadata endpoints (`http://169.254.169.254/`) that hand out credentials, or use the
server to attack other hosts. A URL with an absolute address also replaces an `HttpClient`'s
`BaseAddress`.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the client sends the full URL that the server fetches.

```csharp
using System.Net.Http;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class PreviewController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly HttpClient _http;

    public PreviewController(HttpClient http) => _http = http;

    [HttpGet]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Get([FromQuery] string url)
    {
        var html = await _http.GetStringAsync(url);
        return Content(html, "text/plain");
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** the origin is fixed and the request only names an article in its path.

```csharp
using System.Net.Http;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class PreviewController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly HttpClient _http;

    public PreviewController(HttpClient http) => _http = http;

    [HttpGet]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Get([FromQuery] string article)
    {
        var html = await _http.GetStringAsync("https://news.example.com/articles/" + Uri.EscapeDataString(article));
        return Content(html, "text/plain");
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep the scheme and host fixed: build the URL from a constant origin that ends with a path
  separator (`"https://api.example.com/"`) and put request data only in the path or the query,
  encoded with `Uri.EscapeDataString`.
- With `IHttpClientFactory`, configure the `BaseAddress` of a named or typed client and pass a
  relative path such as `$"v1/items/{id}"`; an absolute URL from the request would replace the
  base address.
- If users must give a URL (webhooks, previews), parse it with `Uri.TryCreate`, allow only `https`,
  compare the host with an allow-list, and resolve and refuse private and link-local addresses.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- ASP.NET Core MVC and Web API
- ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs
- ASP.NET Core Razor Pages
- HttpClient (System.Net.Http)

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
Under `qualor dotnet end`, Qualor's Roslyn taint engine runs this rule in OpenGrep's place, on the
projects the build compiled. It follows request data across methods, files and projects, through
properties, expression-bodied members and services registered for dependency injection, and into the
code of compiled Razor views and pages (`.cshtml`), and it reads all C# the compiler accepts. A
finding is of high confidence, or medium ("Possible" in Qualor) when its path goes through data
stored earlier in the request, a lookup by a request key, or a call or view the engine could not
narrow down. The engine's own limits are listed in the [models' README](../../../models/README.md),
section "Known limits". The bullets below are the OpenGrep rule's: it runs outside
`qualor dotnet end`, on C# files no compiled project covers, and as the fallback when the engine
cannot finish.

- Taint is followed through the methods of one file, not into other files. Request data read
  inside an expression-bodied method (`=> ...`) or a property getter is missed.
- Minimal APIs: a class or record parameter bound from the JSON body without `[FromBody]` is not
  taken for request data, and a handler that is a method of another class is missed. A controller
  named `*Controller` whose base class has another name is missed.
- An enum parameter is reported when the enum is declared after its use or in another file. Only
  allow-lists written as `static readonly` tables of literals count; an equality check or
  `Enumerable.Contains(...)` called as a static method does not, and a variable assigned again
  after a check still counts as checked.
- The value of an awaited `GetXxxAsync`, `FindXxxAsync` or `LoadXxxAsync` call on another object
  (a record found by an id) is taken for stored data, so a URL saved in it is not reported; such a
  method that only hands request data back is missed. Without `await`, the looked-up value still
  counts as request data.
- A host allow-list check (`if (!AllowedHosts.Contains(uri.Host)) return ...;`) is not
  recognised: the URL is still reported after it.
- A fixed origin is recognised when it is written in place as the first part of the URL; an origin
  held in a constant or read from configuration is not, so request data after it is still
  reported.
- `HttpClient` calls are checked on receivers known to be an `HttpClient`; a client reached through
  a wrapper or a generated API client is missed.
- OpenGrep 1.30 does not parse some newer C# syntax (raw strings with `$$"""`, types declared
  without a body such as `class X : Y;`, some multi-line collection expressions); code in those
  parts of a file may be missed.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/csharp/ssrf/ssrf.cs`](../../../rules/csharp/ssrf/ssrf.cs) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.
